keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Augsburg row). The page: 'The prince-bishopric covered some 2365 km2 and had approximately 100,000 inhabitants' (tied to the annexation to Bavaria); it names only Dillingen, Füssen, Straubing (the gift of Bishop Bruno's inheritance, 1006-1020) and no boundary. A 22 km circle at Dillingen (10.32E 48.57N, about 1,520 km2) and a 14 km circle at Füssen (10.70E 47.57N, about 615 km2) give about 2,135 km2, soft. Dated acquisitions are not drawn separately; the city of Augsburg (a free imperial city from 1276) is excluded.

ledger.note: About 888: imperial immediacy. Infobox 'Gained territory and thus, Imperial immediacy: c. 888' (bishopric established in the 4th century).

region.text: the temporal lands of the bishops of Augsburg

ledger.note: From 1248 (page gives only the episcopate 1248-1286): Dillingen. 'The town and castle of Dillingen' were bequeathed to the church by Bishop Hartmann (episcopate 1248-1286). Entered at the start of his episcopate as the earliest year the page allows.

region.text: the town and castle of Dillingen

ledger.note: From 1309 (page gives only the episcopate 1309-1331): Füssen. Frederick I 'acquired for his see the castle and stronghold of Füssen.' Entered at the start of his episcopate as the earliest year the page allows.

region.text: the castle and stronghold of Füssen

ledger.note: 1537: Dillingen becomes the residence. 'The bishop withdrew with the cathedral chapter to Dillingen' (the infobox gives 'Capital: Augsburg, to 1276; Dillingen an der Donau').

1632: the Swedes. Infobox 'Occupied by Sweden: 1632-1635'; Gustavus Adolphus's occupation of Augsburg began in 1632. The page speaks of the city (a free city) and not of the bishop's lands; the region is the stand-in for the prince-bishopric.
1635: imperial troops relieve Augsburg (infobox 'Occupied by Sweden: 1632-1635'). The Edict of Restitution (1629) had restored much of the former diocesan property.

25 February 1803: mediatised to Bavaria (infobox). 'In 1802, by an act of the Delegation of the Perpetual Imperial Diet (Reichsdeputationsrezess)' the territory was assigned to Bavaria; the Elector 'took possession of it on 1 December 1802'. The two dates are not reconciled on the page.

certainty.note: The page gives a total area (2,365 km2) and names two places; the two circles are stand-ins and nothing of the lands before 1248 is known.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Augsburg row.

SCOPE. Infobox 'c. 888' (imperial immediacy) to 25 February 1803 (mediatised to Bavaria). The page's 'Bishopric established: 4th century' is the diocese, not the state. The free imperial city of Augsburg (1276) is not part of the prince-bishopric and is not drawn. The 1537 Dillingen move and the infobox 'Capital: Augsburg, to 1276' conflict; the text event is used.

SHAPES. Dillingen 10.32E 48.57N 22 km; Fussen 10.70E 47.57N 14 km (about 2,135 km2 against 2,365 km2 on the page). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Dillingen an der Donau', 'Fussen'. Straubing is named as a gift of Bishop Bruno (1006-1020) and is not drawn (the Straubing in the page is not placed).

NOT SETTLED. (1) Both acquisitions are dated by episcopate only (confidence 1); (2) the page gives the Reformation losses ('about 250 parishes, 24 monasteries, and over 500 benefices', no year) and the Westphalia losses (1648) without land, so none is drawn; (3) whether the Swedish occupation covered the bishop's lands (the page speaks of Augsburg city); (4) Bavarian possession 1 December 1802 against the infobox's 25 February 1803.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
